passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Maintain justice and do what is right, for My salvation is coming soon, and My righteousness will be revealed.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD commands His people.
The LORD says, "Maintain justice."
The LORD says, "Do what is right."
The LORD promises salvation.
The LORD says, "My salvation is coming soon."
The LORD promises to reveal His righteousness.
The LORD says, "My righteousness will be revealed."
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שִׁמְר֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וַעֲשׂ֣וּ צְדָקָ֑ה כִּֽי־ קְרוֹבָ֤ה יְשֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לָב֔וֹא וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לְהִגָּלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God blesses the person who obeys Him.
This person does what is right.
This person holds tightly to what is good.
This person keeps the Sabbath holy.
He does not profane the Sabbath.
He keeps his hand from doing any evil.
God calls this person blessed.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֤י אֱנוֹשׁ֙ יַעֲשֶׂה־ זֹּ֔את וּבֶן־ אָדָ֖ם יַחֲזִ֣יק בָּ֑הּ שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וְשֹׁמֵ֥ר יָד֖וֹ מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּל־ רָֽע׃ס

passages.text: Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, “The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people.” And let the eunuch not say, “I am but a dry tree.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to foreigners who join themselves to Him.
A foreigner is a person from another nation.
A foreigner who joins himself to the LORD must not say, “The LORD will separate me from His people.”
The LORD also speaks to eunuchs.
A eunuch is a man who cannot have children.
A eunuch must not say, “I am a dry tree.”
A dry tree cannot produce fruit or children.
The LORD tells both foreigners and eunuchs not to think they are excluded from His people.
passages.original: וְאַל־ יֹאמַ֣ר בֶּן־ הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוָ֤ה אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַבְדֵּ֧ל יַבְדִּילַ֛נִי יְהוָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל עַמּ֑וֹ וְאַל־ יֹאמַר֙ הַסָּרִ֔יס הֵ֥ן אֲנִ֖י עֵ֥ץ יָבֵֽשׁ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, who choose what pleases Me and hold fast to My covenant— I will give them, in My house and within My walls, a memorial and a name better than that of sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the eunuchs.
These eunuchs keep the LORD’s Sabbaths.
They choose what pleases the LORD.
They hold fast to the LORD’s covenant.
The LORD will give these eunuchs a place in His house.
He will give them a place within His walls.
He will give them a memorial and a name.
This name will be better than sons and daughters.
The LORD will give them an everlasting name.
No one will cut off this name.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַסָּֽרִיסִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁמְרוּ֙ אֶת־ שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֔י וּבָֽחֲר֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑צְתִּי וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃ וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֜ם בְּבֵיתִ֤י וּבְחֽוֹמֹתַי֙ יָ֣ד וָשֵׁ֔ם ט֖וֹב מִבָּנִ֣ים וּמִבָּנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם עוֹלָם֙ אֶתֶּן־ ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת׃ס

passages.text: And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to minister to Him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be His servants— all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and who hold fast to My covenant— I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”
passages.sermon:
Foreigners can join themselves to the LORD.
These foreigners serve the LORD.
They love the name of the LORD.
They become His servants.
They keep the Sabbath.
They do not profane the Sabbath.
They hold fast to the LORD’s covenant.
The LORD will bring these people to His holy mountain.
The LORD will make them joyful in His house of prayer.
The LORD will accept their burnt offerings on His altar.
The LORD will accept their sacrifices on His altar.
The LORD’s house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֣י הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עַל־ יְהוָה֙ לְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וּֽלְאַהֲבָה֙ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לִהְי֥וֹת ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים כָּל־ שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃ וַהֲבִיאוֹתִ֞ים אֶל־ הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֗י וְשִׂמַּחְתִּים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית תְּפִלָּתִ֔י עוֹלֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְזִבְחֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָצ֖וֹן עַֽל־ מִזְבְּחִ֑י כִּ֣י בֵיתִ֔י בֵּית־ תְּפִלָּ֥ה יִקָּרֵ֖א לְכָל־ הָעַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: Thus declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel: “I will gather to them still others besides those already gathered.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD gathers the people of Israel who have been scattered.
The Lord GOD says, “I will gather more people to Israel.
I will add others to those who are already gathered.”
passages.original: נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מְקַבֵּ֖ץ נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֛וֹד אֲקַבֵּ֥ץ עָלָ֖יו לְנִקְבָּצָֽיו׃

passages.text: Come, all you beasts of the field; eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest.
passages.sermon:
God calls to the wild animals.
He speaks to every beast of the field.
He commands them to come.
He tells them to eat.
He calls every beast of the forest.
He invites them to eat freely.
passages.original: כֹּ֖ל חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י אֵתָ֕יוּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל כָּל־ חַיְת֖וֹ בַּיָּֽעַר׃ס

passages.text: Israel’s watchmen are blind, they are all oblivious; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; they are dreamers lying around, loving to slumber.
passages.sermon:
Israel’s watchmen are blind.
They do not see danger.
They do not understand what is happening.
All the watchmen are unaware.
They are like mute dogs.
These dogs cannot bark.
They cannot warn anyone.
The watchmen are dreamers.
They lie around.
They love to sleep.
passages.original: צָפוּ עִוְרִ֤ים כֻּלָּם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ כֻּלָּם֙ כְּלָבִ֣ים אִלְּמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לִנְבֹּ֑חַ הֹזִים֙ שֹֽׁכְבִ֔ים אֹהֲבֵ֖י לָנֽוּם׃

passages.text: Like ravenous dogs, they are never satisfied. They are shepherds with no discernment; they all turn to their own way, each one seeking his own gain: “Come, let me get the wine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorrow will be like today, only far better!”
passages.sermon:
Israel’s leaders act like greedy dogs.
These leaders never feel satisfied.
They serve as shepherds, but they lack understanding.
Each leader follows his own path.
Every leader seeks his own profit.
They say, “Come, let me get wine.”
They say, “Let us drink strong drink.”
They say, “Tomorrow will be like today.”
They say, “Tomorrow will be even greater.”
passages.original: וְהַכְּלָבִ֣ים עַזֵּי־ נֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א יָֽדְעוּ֙ שָׂבְעָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה רֹעִ֔ים לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ הָבִ֑ין כֻּלָּם֙ לְדַרְכָּ֣ם פָּנ֔וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְבִצְע֖וֹ מִקָּצֵֽהוּ׃ אֵתָ֥יוּ אֶקְחָה־ יַ֖יִן וְנִסְבְּאָ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְהָיָ֤ה כָזֶה֙ י֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר גָּד֖וֹל יֶ֥תֶר מְאֹֽד׃
